- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 2.5), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 15–30% for 3–7 day horizon.
- Model frequently fails to capture mean reversion in 10–15 day horizon; if history shows oscillation around 2.0–2.2, forecast should be anchored near that range.
- For 30-day horizon, model often ignores sentiment trend; if sentiment is trending upward, add 5–10% bias to forecast; if trending downward, subtract 5–10%.
- Overshoots in 30-day forecasts are common when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in final 5–7 days.
